draft.overall: NXL leads the covered gainers into power hour, up 68 percent from the prior close, with fresh news in our sources: a 10-year exclusive distribution and local-manufacturing agreement for Brazil and South America. NAMM is next by move, up 51 percent and printing a new high of day since the previous checkpoint, after first-half 2026 results and an operating update, while EJH is up 28 percent with an AI service robot launch found alongside a private-placement agreement. Fresh news turned up in our sources for 6 of the 12 names the desk covers.

lines.text: Nexalin announced at 08:30 ET on October 1, 2026 a definitive 10-year exclusive distribution and local-manufacturing agreement covering Brazil and South America, which the company framed as a move toward commercial revenue; the desk reads it as a company-specific commercialization story, with secondary coverage tying it to a large stock gain on heavy volume. Contract value, minimum purchases and expected revenue are not stated, and any approval or readiness conditions before revenue are not established.

This is not a fresh catalyst: the latest item found is the September 3, 2026 retail launch of Perfecta plant-based meat in the Northeastern U.S., its first U.S. shelf placement, with no sales, revenue or store-count figure disclosed. Our sources hold no later company announcement tied to this session.

Airship AI announced at 09:00 ET on October 1, 2026 firm-fixed-price, brand-name-only contract awards worth $29.0M from an agency within the Department of Homeland Security, which the desk reads as material against its recently reported quarterly revenue. Delivery timing, revenue-recognition timing and the specific agency are not established.

The company's S-3 shelf registration for up to $50.0M of common stock, preferred stock and warrants became effective on September 30, 2026; the desk reads this as financing capacity only, with no takedown, pricing or completed sale in our sources. It is down 17.4% since the previous checkpoint, and nothing found ties the shelf to the price move.

The pro forma effect on revenue, earnings and cash, and the odds of receiving the earnout, are not known.

Product details and revenue expectations are not in our sources, and the placement's closing is not established.
